author: Greg McVerry
body_html:
@bali_maha So sorry this is causing you and your daughter stress. Reading should never cause harm.

I am hoping the teacher has good intentions as we need a bit more to call this competition. Were kids getting ranked? publicly shamed? Being assessed outloud in front of peers?

Speed reading test at a early grade are often used as we know fluency is a great predictor of later literacy outcomes. Yet this data should not be used as a competition but rather as a marker of growth and in some cases, an indicator students need additional support.

I do not really worry about fluency rates until about 3rd grade (8-9 in USA). If students are not reading: "grade level" fluently by then I might have a conversation with parents. Many disagree with me and worry about fluency starting around 5-6....makes little sense to me

I think your daughter's teacher may be trying to measure fluency, "speed, accuracy, and prosody." Getting people to read faster does actually improve their reading but any time a measure of reading reduces the motivation to read it does more harm than good.

If the kids were getting ranked, publicly shamed, or being assessed out loud in front of peers then any validity in a fluency assessment is gone.
